stemMd: An object is placed 30 cm from a thin converging lens of focal length 10 cm. Using the thin-lens formula, how far from the lens is the real image?
explanationMd: Use 1/f=1/object distance+1/image distance. Thus 1/image distance=1/10−1/30=1/15, giving 15 cm. The object lies beyond twice the focal length, so the image lies between one and two focal lengths.

distractorRationale.e: Equal object and image distances occur at twice the focal length.
distractorRationale.d: This simply subtracts focal length from object distance.
distractorRationale.b: This incorrectly adds reciprocal distances before inverting.
